note: Seljuk expansion into Armenia and Anatolia brought the sultanate into sustained conflict with Byzantium. Manzikert (1071) was the decisive moment: the capture of Emperor Romanos IV opened Anatolia to Turkic settlement. Byzantine Emperor Manuel I's defeat at Myriokephalon (1176) ended any prospect of reconquest.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Seljuk victory at Manzikert (1071) and subsequent Anatolian settlement stripped Byzantium of its main military recruiting ground and agricultural tax base in a single decade; the resulting imperial weakness forced Alexios I's appeal to Rome (1095), which directly launched the First Crusade—making the Seljuk-Byzantine rivalry the indirect cause of two centuries of crusading activity in the Levant.
